claim: The rule that an empty event_types subscribes an endpoint to every event type exists only as the inline expression `not endpoint.event_types or event_type in endpoint.event_types` inside enqueue_for_event, with no named helper or test, while docs/webhooks.md states it as a customer-facing contract.

enqueue_for_event matches event_type against endpoint.event_types with an exact `in` comparison over unvalidated JSONB content, so the match is case- and whitespace-sensitive and becomes a substring test if the stored value is a bare string rather than a list.
run_worker awaits asyncio.sleep(poll_interval) only when the claimed batch was empty, so after a non-empty batch the loop immediately re-acquires the lock and re-queries with no delay.

run_worker's `if not batch: await asyncio.sleep(poll_interval)` sits after the finally that deletes LOCK_KEY, so the empty-batch back-off is taken with the lock already released and the loop re-acquires the lock once per poll.

enqueue_for_event, _claim_batch and _finish write through session_scope with no flush or commit of their own, relying on the scope's commit-on-exit semantics, while create_webhook_endpoint in the same change calls session.flush() explicitly.

WebhookDelivery.to_dict calls self.next_attempt_at.isoformat() with no None guard, unlike the sibling fields it passes through raw, so serializing a row whose next_attempt_at is unset raises AttributeError.

The ForeignKey declarations on WebhookEndpoint.org_id and WebhookDelivery.endpoint_id omit ondelete="CASCADE" while migration 0042 declares ON DELETE CASCADE, so the ORM-level delete behaviour and any schema built from the model metadata differ from the migration's DDL.

An empty WebhookEndpoint.event_types list is the column default at both the model and the SQL level and is also read by enqueue_for_event as "subscribe to every event type", so one in-band value carries both "not configured yet" and "send everything".
Each WebhookDelivery row stores its own full copy of the event payload, so an event fanned out to N endpoints persists N copies of the payload in addition to the one on the event row.
An empty event_types list is an in-band sentinel that enqueue_for_event reads as "deliver every event type", colliding with the same value's legitimate meaning of subscribing to nothing.

The three new route handlers are declared async def while their bodies perform only synchronous blocking session_scope/session.query work, so FastAPI runs that database work on the event loop instead of in the threadpool a def handler would get.

create_webhook_endpoint builds and returns endpoint.to_dict() after session.flush() but before session_scope commits, so the 201 body including the id and signing secret is produced from an uncommitted row.
create_webhook_endpoint's response is built inside the session_scope block and survives only because to_dict() materializes plain values before the commit expires the instance's attributes.

create_webhook_endpoint performs only a syntactic URL check and never probes the registered endpoint, so a 201 and a signing secret are returned for a URL that every delivery attempt will fail against.
signing.verify is exported and covered by tests but is called by no production code path in the change, so nothing under app/ inbound-verifies a webhook signature.
